title: Tragedy in Greece as Firefighting Helicopters Collide During Wildfire Crisis
subtitle: Two crew members died after a mid-air collision while battling dangerous fires near Athens.

summary.en: Two firefighting helicopters collided in mid-air while working to stop wildfires near Athens, Greece. Two crew members, a Danish pilot and a Greek officer, were killed in the crash. Two other crew members, including a British pilot, survived the accident. The incident happened during a period of extreme weather with very strong winds. Greek officials have grounded all helicopters of the same type while they investigate the situation.
summary.zh: 兩架消防直升機在希臘雅典附近執行滅火任務時於空中相撞。兩名機組人員，包括一名丹麥籍飛行員與一名希臘官員，在墜機中喪生。另外兩名機組人員，包括一名英國籍飛行員，則在事故中倖存。這起事件發生在強風肆虐的極端天氣期間。希臘官員已下令同型號直升機全面停飛，以調查事故情況。

paragraphs.en: A tragic accident occurred on Sunday as two firefighting helicopters collided in mid-air while battling large wildfires in Greece. The incident took place approximately 65 kilometers west of Athens, near the Psatha area. According to BBC News, the collision happened while the aircraft were working to control a fire burning on the border of the Attica and Boeotia regions.
paragraphs.zh: 週日發生了一起悲劇性事故，兩架消防直升機在希臘執行大型野火滅火任務時於空中相撞。事故地點位於雅典以西約六十五公里處，靠近普薩塔（Psatha）地區。根據英國廣播公司新聞（BBC News）報導，這起碰撞發生在兩架飛機於阿提卡（Attica）與維奧蒂亞（Boeotia）地區交界處進行滅火作業時。

paragraphs.en: Video footage of the event showed one of the helicopters hitting the propellers of the other. The damaged aircraft then caught fire and crashed into a ravine. The second helicopter managed to make an emergency landing in an area with low vegetation. The Greek fire service confirmed that the two crew members on the crashed helicopter—a Danish pilot and a Greek fire service liaison officer—were found unconscious and later pronounced dead. The two people on the second aircraft, a British pilot and another Greek coordinator, survived the crash with minor injuries. They were taken to a hospital for observation, as reported by BBC News.
paragraphs.zh: 現場影片顯示，其中一架直升機撞上了另一架的螺旋槳。受損的飛機隨後起火並墜入峽谷。第二架直升機則成功在植被稀疏的區域緊急迫降。希臘消防部門證實，墜毀直升機上的兩名機組人員——一名丹麥籍飛行員與一名希臘消防聯絡官——被發現時已失去意識，隨後宣告不治。第二架飛機上的兩名人員，包括一名英國籍飛行員與另一名希臘協調員，在墜機事故中倖存並受輕傷。根據英國廣播公司新聞報導，他們已被送往醫院接受觀察。

paragraphs.en: This accident is a major setback for emergency teams currently facing what officials describe as a "titanic battle" against nature. The Greek Prime Minister, Kyriakos Mitsotakis, expressed his deep sadness over the loss of the crew members. Following the crash, authorities grounded all Bell helicopters across the country as part of standard safety protocol, according to information provided to the BBC. The British pilot involved was a private contractor hired for the wildfire season and was not part of an international aid exchange.
paragraphs.zh: 這起事故對目前正處於官員所稱「與大自然進行艱苦搏鬥」的緊急救援團隊而言，是一次重大打擊。希臘總理米佐塔基斯（Kyriakos Mitsotakis）對機組人員的殉職表達了深切哀悼。根據提供給英國廣播公司的資訊，事故發生後，當局已依據標準安全程序，下令全國所有貝爾（Bell）直升機停飛。涉事的英國籍飛行員是為野火季節聘請的私人承包商，並非國際援助交流計畫的一員。

paragraphs.en: Greece is currently dealing with a series of intense wildfires that have forced mass evacuations. The situation has been made much worse by extreme weather conditions. According to The Guardian, gale-force winds—very strong winds—have pushed flames toward settlements on the western edges of Athens. These winds have reached speeds of over 125 kilometers per hour, making it extremely dangerous for firefighting aircraft to operate. The Greek civil protection minister, Evangelos Tournas, noted that the fire department has been pushed to its limits. He explained that the high winds make it difficult for aircraft to draw water or safely drop it on the fires due to extreme turbulence.
paragraphs.zh: 希臘目前正應對一系列導致大規模撤離的猛烈野火。極端天氣條件使情況變得更加嚴峻。根據《衛報》（The Guardian）報導，強勁的陣風將火焰推向雅典西郊的住宅區。這些風速超過每小時一百二十五公里，使得消防飛機的作業極度危險。希臘公民保護部長圖納斯（Evangelos Tournas）指出，消防部門已達到極限。他解釋說，強風導致極端亂流，使得飛機難以取水或安全地將水投放到火場上。

paragraphs.en: Beyond the capital, the wildfire crisis has affected many parts of the country, including the islands of Cephalonia and Crete, as well as the southern Peloponnese. Deutsche Welle (DW) reported that over 6,500 hectares of land have been burned in the areas around the Gulf of Corinth alone. In response to the growing threat, more than 500 firefighters and forest commandos have been working to keep the flames away from homes. In nearby villages, police have been going door-to-door to urge residents to leave their homes for safety.
paragraphs.zh: 除了首都之外，野火危機已波及全國多地，包括凱法利尼亞島（Cephalonia）、克里特島（Crete）以及南部的伯羅奔尼撒（Peloponnese）地區。德國之聲（DW）報導稱，僅在科林斯灣（Gulf of Corinth）周邊地區，就有超過六千五百公頃的土地被燒毀。為應對日益嚴重的威脅，超過五百名消防員與森林特種部隊正努力將火焰阻擋在住宅區外。在附近的村莊，警方正挨家挨戶勸導居民撤離家園以確保安全。

paragraphs.en: This week has been particularly difficult for Greece, as three other firefighters have died in the line of duty in recent days. While most wildfires are started by humans, either by accident or on purpose, experts point out that climate change is creating conditions that make these fires more common and more dangerous. A mild, wet winter encouraged plants to grow, which then dried out during the recent heatwaves, creating large amounts of fuel for the fires. Additionally, authorities are investigating potential arson. Deutsche Welle (DW) reported that a 44-year-old man was arrested on suspicion of deliberately starting a fire on the island of Cephalonia.
paragraphs.zh: 本週對希臘而言格外艱難，因為近日還有另外三名消防員在執行任務時殉職。雖然大多數野火是由人為因素引起，無論是意外還是蓄意縱火，專家指出氣候變遷正在創造讓這些火災變得更頻繁且更危險的條件。溫和潮濕的冬季促進了植物生長，隨後在近期的熱浪中變得乾燥，為火災提供了大量燃料。此外，當局正在調查潛在的縱火行為。德國之聲報導稱，一名四十四歲男子因涉嫌在凱法利尼亞島蓄意縱火而被捕。

paragraphs.en: As the country continues to fight these blazes, officials are warning that the coming days will remain "extremely difficult." While other European nations like France and Spain have begun to contain their own major fires, the situation in Greece remains critical. The combination of dry land, high temperatures, and powerful winds continues to challenge the brave men and women working on the front lines. For now, the focus remains on protecting lives and preventing the fires from reaching more populated areas as the investigation into the helicopter collision continues.
paragraphs.zh: 隨著該國持續對抗這些火勢，官員警告未來幾天仍將「極度艱難」。儘管法國與西班牙等其他歐洲國家已開始控制各自境內的大型火災，但希臘的情況依然危急。乾燥的土地、高溫與強風的結合，持續考驗著在第一線工作的勇敢男女。目前，在針對直升機碰撞事故進行調查的同時，重點仍放在保護生命安全，並防止火勢蔓延至更多人口稠密地區。

keyTerms.definitionEn: A problem that delays or prevents progress.
keyTerms.noteZh: 此詞常被誤認為是動詞片語，但在文中作為名詞，指代導致任務進度受阻的意外。文中：This accident is a major setback for emergency teams currently facing what officials describe as a "titanic battle" against nature.

keyTerms.definitionEn: To prevent an aircraft or its crew from flying.
keyTerms.noteZh: 常見作名詞（地面），這裡作動詞，指禁止飛機飛行。文中：Following the crash, authorities grounded all Bell helicopters across the country as part of standard safety protocol, according to information provided to the BBC.

keyTerms.definitionEn: While performing one's official job responsibilities.
keyTerms.definitionZh: 在執行公務時、在職責範圍內。
keyTerms.noteZh: 此片語描述在工作期間發生的不幸事件，非字面上的「線」。文中：This week has been particularly difficult for Greece, as three other firefighters have died in the line of duty in recent days.

More than 300 firefighters are working to stop the flames from spreading further. Strong winds have made it very difficult for aircraft to help with the firefighting efforts. Officials have confirmed that homes have been damaged and the environmental impact is severe. This situation is part of a larger, record-breaking summer of fires across Europe.

Experts warn that the situation remains dangerous as high temperatures continue to threaten several regions.

quiz.question: What happened to the crew members of the two helicopters involved in the collision?

options.A: All four individuals on the two aircraft lost their lives in the crash.
options.B: The two crew members on the helicopter that crashed died, while the two on the other aircraft survived.
options.C: Both pilots died, but the two fire service coordinators survived with minor injuries.
options.D: All four individuals survived the crash, though two were hospitalized for observation.

quiz.explanationZh: 正確答案為 B。根據文章第二段，墜毀直升機上的兩名機組人員（丹麥籍飛行員與希臘籍聯絡官）被發現時已無意識且隨後宣告死亡；而另一架迫降的直升機上的兩人（英國籍飛行員與另一名希臘籍協調員）則受輕傷生還。選項 A 錯誤，因為只有墜毀那架的機組員死亡；選項 C 錯誤，因為死亡的是一名飛行員與一名聯絡官，而非兩名飛行員；選項 D 錯誤，因為明確指出有兩人死亡。

quiz.question: Based on the information provided, why are the current wildfires in Greece particularly challenging to control?

options.A: There is a severe shortage of international aid and firefighting equipment available to Greece.
options.B: The fires are primarily located in remote, unreachable areas far from any settlements.
options.C: A combination of environmental factors and weather conditions has created an environment where fires spread easily and are difficult to fight.
options.D: The firefighting teams have been grounded indefinitely due to the recent helicopter accident.

quiz.explanationZh: 正確答案為 C。文章第四段提到強風與極端天氣，第六段提到氣候變遷導致植物生長後乾枯成為燃料，這些因素共同使得火勢更難控制。選項 A 錯誤，文中未提到缺乏國際援助；選項 B 與文章提到火勢威脅到村莊及雅典邊緣的情況相反；選項 D 錯誤，文中僅提到 Bell 直升機被停飛進行安全檢查，並非所有消防團隊都停擺。

quiz.question: In the third paragraph, what does the author mean by describing the firefighting effort as a 'titanic battle'?

options.A: A battle involving many different countries working together.
options.B: A conflict that is extremely large, difficult, and intense.
options.C: A fight that is primarily happening near the sea or water.
options.D: A struggle that is doomed to fail because of the forces of nature.

quiz.explanationZh: 正確答案為 B。在文中，「titanic」源自希臘神話的泰坦巨神，在此處被用作形容詞，意指規模巨大、艱鉅且極具挑戰性的鬥爭。選項 A 與國際援助無關；選項 C 是對「titanic」字面意義的誤解；選項 D 雖然提到困難，但「titanic」本身強調的是規模與強度，而非預設失敗的結局。

quiz.question: What is the primary focus of this article?

options.A: To analyze the legal consequences of arson in Greece.
options.B: To report on the tragic helicopter accident during the ongoing Greek wildfire crisis.
options.C: To explain the history of firefighting techniques used in the Mediterranean region.
options.D: To criticize the Greek government's response to the recent heatwaves.

quiz.explanationZh: 正確答案為 B。本文開篇即報導了直升機相撞事故，隨後將此事件置於希臘當前嚴峻的森林大火背景中討論，涵蓋了事故細節、氣候因素及火災對國家的影響。選項 A 僅是文章最後一段提到的小細節；選項 C 完全未在文中討論；選項 D 雖然提到政府官員的行動，但文章旨在客觀報導災情與事故，並非專門批評政府。
